code_findings.title: When ReactDOMForm-test.js is run by the repository's Jest setup, the newly added focused case excludes the file's ordinary sibling tests from that run.
code_findings.explanation: The change adds `it.only`, and repository evidence explicitly identifies `.only` as the mechanism for focusing a test. The focused-test helper delegates to `test.only`, while the ESLint rule that would reject focused tests is disabled. Thus this is not merely an ordinary added test: it selects the new case over non-focused sibling cases in ReactDOMForm-test.js.
code_findings.impact: Caused by the change: The changed line introduces the only focused marker in this file. The repository uses `.only` to focus tests and does not enable its no-focused-tests lint rule, so this new marker causes Jest to select this case rather than the file's ordinary `it` cases, reducing execution of the form regression suite.

pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: React's form-transition hook initialization now distinguishes a fully upgraded form fiber from one that merely has a single existing hook. The accompanying focused test targets two rapid submissions while the first asynchronous form action is still pending and expects both actions to run without an exception.

behavior_changes.description: When a form fiber has one existing state hook but no following hook, it is no longer treated as already fully stateful. This is intended to let two closely spaced submissions of the same form both invoke the asynchronous form action without throwing; the regression test observes two action invocations.
evidence: The early-return condition now requires both an existing hook and a following hook.
The new test submits the same form twice with a delay while each action remains asynchronous, then expects two action calls.

important_symbols.reason: This is the sole production-code change. Its hook-list test determines whether form transition state is reused or initialization continues.
The changed helper is adjacent to and apparently used by host-transition processing, making this the relevant internal call path for understanding which form operations encounter the new condition.
The test provides the clearest supplied evidence of the intended externally observable case: two overlapping form submissions should invoke the action twice without failing.
